messages.subject: setSeed default not FALSE?
parts: Hello. Apologies if this has already been answered. I am running v0.12.1 and using the `nimbleMCMC` function to run a model. I tried to implement parallel processing of two chains without any additional programming by simply running a single chain in two separate instances of R with the intention of combining them later into an `mcmc.list` object to calculate relevant convergence metrics. I did not specify any value for `setSeed`, so based on documentation I am seeing, I assume the default value is FALSE, and so a different seed should be assigned for each chain. When the chains finished, however, the posterior samples are identical. I assume I can actually deliberately set two different seeds to get two independent chains, although I have not tried that. Am I misunderstanding how this works? Is there an explanation for why I am not getting independent chains from two separate instances of R?

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: setSeed default not FALSE?
parts:
My suspicion is that each session of R began with the same initial random number seed, as R does unless you specify a new seed.  Thus, with (the default value of) setSeed = FALSE, and I'm assuming also identical initial values for each R session also, each MCMC chain proceeded identically.  Is that plausible?

In any case, you could provide one chain with setSeed = 1, and the other with setSeed = 2, and they will begin with those different seeds, and should thereafter not be identical.

Hope this helps,
Daniel

messages.subject: RE: setSeed default not FALSE?
parts:
Thanks! I realized after posting that I had this same problem for another analysis not involving NIMBLE. I used ‘rm(.Random.seed, envir=.GlobalEnv)’ to remove R’s default seed from the environment. It seems to work for NIMBLE as well.
